_about: Seesaws and spinning platforms - the bodies the original pins with a revolute
joint. Almost nothing is authored here, because almost nothing is ours: the
converter already carries the eight joint_* keys and the revoluteJoint name
through to each placement, and the engine's own solver does the rest.
Hinge.hpp says how the anchor and the angle are worked out.

_note: How much of the joint's error the solver takes out per step. The engine's own
default, carried as data so a level that jitters can be retuned without
touching code. Zero lets a loaded hinge drift apart; above one it

_motors_not_built: All ten placements carry joint_enable_motor 0, and ETHCallback_spinning_platform
(bytes 371942..372140) fetches the joint every frame and sets its motor speed to
zero besides. So these are free-swinging bodies with angle limits and nothing
level21b's motor_seesaw carries metadata/motorSpeed = -4 and joint_motor_speed
-5 with the motor disabled, and nothing in the bytecode reads either. Authored
and unread, like the carranca's dirX magnitude.
_spinning_cross_not_built: ETHCallback_spinning_cross (bytes 371655..371816) turns its body at a constant
0.6 rad/s. No converted level places a spinning_cross, so there is nothing to
turn. Recorded rather than built, and the day a level places one this is the
note that says what it should do.
_motor_seesaw_unexplained: level21b's motor_seesaw is limited to 0 .. 1.5708 - pinned at one end of its own
range - with no motor and no callback. A seesaw that can only fall one way is a
plausible puzzle and also plausibly means something drives it that has not been
found. It is chapter 3 and gates nothing in chapter 2; written down rather than
reasoned backwards from the assumption that it must work somehow.
